aspects.says: The Filer creates a file once per compile, so an aggregate file written in every round with annotations fails with FilerException once a later round brings more; collecting across rounds and writing once fixes it.
basis: section:The Filer Creates Each File Once and Never Replaces a Class That Exists

aspects.says: javac 25 runs no processor it finds only on the class path, where javac 21 ran it with a note; a build names the processor or a processor path.
basis: section:A Processor Is Code javac Runs During the Compile, and What It Adds Is New Source Files

aspects.says: A Messager ERROR passed the element makes javac report the user's file and line and fails the compile; an error left to the generated code points at a file the developer never wrote.
basis: section:An Error Reported at the Element Makes javac Point at the User's Line

aspects.says: A processor runs inside javac, reads declarations through javax.lang.model rather than Class objects, and adds new source files through the Filer that are compiled with the sources.
basis: section:A Processor Is Code javac Runs During the Compile, and What It Adds Is New Source Files

aspects.says: An ERROR printed without an element has no file or line, and an exception thrown from process stops javac with a stack trace.
basis: section:An Error Reported at the Element Makes javac Point at the User's Line

aspects.says: A processor can't replace or edit a class in the sources: the Filer treats the inputs as already created and Element has only getters; Lombok works through javac internals instead.
basis: section:The Filer Creates Each File Once and Never Replaces a Class That Exists

aspects.says: Files generated in one round are the inputs of the next round, a processor is called in every later round through the last one with processingOver() true, and one processor object serves the whole compile.
basis: section:Processing Runs in Rounds, and a Generated File Is Processed in the Next One
